title: Qatar Income Tax 2026: Take-Home Pay for Expats
h1: Income tax in Qatar (2026): how much of your salary do you keep?
description: Qatar charges no income tax on salary. See what expats keep, what Qatari nationals pay into the GRSIA pension, and the end-of-service gratuity, with examples.
lede: Qatar charges no personal income tax on employment income, so an expat on QAR 240,000 a year keeps the full QAR 240,000. A Qatari national pays 7% of salary into the GRSIA pension fund, QAR 16,800 on the same pay, and keeps QAR 223,200. The employer adds 14% on top for nationals, and expats receive an end-of-service gratuity instead of a pension.

law.intro: The figures are the 2026 rules as the calculator models them. Salary is not taxed for individuals in Qatar. What differs by person is the pension: Qatari nationals contribute through the General Retirement and Social Insurance Authority (GRSIA), and expats do not.

blocks.h3: No personal income tax on salary
blocks.html: Qatar does not tax wages, allowances or bonuses for an individual, so there is no tax bracket and no tax withheld from your payslip. VAT, where a country charges it, is a consumption tax added to what you buy and is not taken from your pay, so it is not part of this calculation.

cite.name: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Qatar: taxes on personal income

blocks.html: The calculator takes 7% of pay from Qatari nationals for the GRSIA pension, on pay up to QAR 100,000 a month. The employer pays 14% on top. The employer share is shown as a cost and does not reduce your pay.

cite.name: Al Meezan, Qatar Social Insurance Law No. 1 of 2022 (GRSIA contributions, 7% employee, cap 100,000 a month)
TRC, Qatar retirement and pension law: 7% employee, 14% employer, QAR 100,000 monthly ceiling

blocks.h3: Expats: no pension, an end-of-service gratuity
blocks.html: Expatriates do not contribute to GRSIA. The employer owes an end-of-service gratuity at the end of the contract, based on basic pay and years of service under the labour law. It is paid once, when you leave.

cite.name: Al Meezan, Qatar Labour Law No. 14 of 2004 (end-of-service gratuity)

examples.title: How much income tax does an expat pay in Qatar on QAR 240,000?
examples.intro: An expat on QAR 240,000 pays no income tax and no pension contribution, so take-home pay is QAR 240,000, or 100% of gross. A raise is kept in full because the marginal rate is 0%.
examples.after: The gratuity arrives from the employer when the contract ends and is not part of this figure.

cite.name: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Qatar: taxes on personal income

examples.title: Take-home pay for a Qatari national on QAR 240,000 after GRSIA
examples.intro: A Qatari national on QAR 240,000 pays no income tax but 7% into the GRSIA pension, QAR 16,800 a year. You keep QAR 223,200, or 93.0% of gross. The employer pays a further 14%, QAR 33,600, on top, which goes into the pension and does not come out of your pay.
examples.after: The 7% is a pension contribution rather than a tax. It applies up to the cap of QAR 100,000 a month.

cite.name: Al Meezan, Qatar Social Insurance Law No. 1 of 2022 (GRSIA contributions, 7% employee, cap 100,000 a month)
TRC, Qatar retirement and pension law: 7% employee, 14% employer, QAR 100,000 monthly ceiling

strategyIntro: These are mainstream, legal ways to handle your pay and tax position.

strategies.h3: Check your home-country tax residency before you move
strategies.html:
Suits: every expat. Zero tax in the Gulf does not always mean zero tax overall: some countries tax citizens on worldwide income, and others treat you as resident until you meet their exit conditions.

Caveat: the rules sit in your home country's law, not in the Gulf state's. Ask your home tax authority or an adviser, and keep records of your move.

strategies.h3: Save and invest the extra take-home yourself
strategies.html:
Suits: expats who keep the whole salary. Without a pension deduction, retirement saving is your own job. Regular contributions to a pension or investment plan in your home country or a low-cost portfolio are the usual route.

Caveat: a gratuity at the end of the contract is not a retirement plan, and where you invest decides the tax on the returns. Use the Financial Freedom Calculator to see how much you need.

strategies.h3: Understand your gratuity before you sign
strategies.html:
Suits: expats comparing offers. The gratuity is your only employer-funded exit benefit, and it depends on basic pay and length of service.

Caveat: a contract with a low basic salary and large allowances can produce a smaller gratuity, so ask how it is calculated.

cite.name: Al Meezan, Qatar Labour Law No. 14 of 2004 (end-of-service gratuity)

limits: Employment income only. It models one salary for a full year, with no other income, bonuses or a part year.
Gratuity not modelled. End-of-service gratuity depends on your basic pay, length of service and contract, so it is not added to the figures.
Home-country tax. The calculator shows only what the Gulf state takes. Your home country may still tax you on worldwide income, depending on its rules and any treaty.
You choose the status. The calculator takes national or expat from you and does not test whether you qualify.
Package versus cash. The calculator takes the gross pay you enter. Housing, schooling or flight allowances in your contract are not split out.

faq.q: How much tax do I pay on QAR 240,000 in Qatar?
faq.a: An expat pays no income tax and keeps QAR 240,000. A Qatari national pays 7% into GRSIA and keeps QAR 223,200. Try your own figure in the Global Income Tax Calculator.

cite.name: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Qatar: taxes on personal income
Al Meezan, Qatar Social Insurance Law No. 1 of 2022 (GRSIA contributions, 7% employee, cap 100,000 a month)

faq.q: What is end-of-service gratuity in Qatar and does it replace a pension?
faq.a: For expats, yes in practice. They are not in the GRSIA pension scheme, so the employer instead pays a lump sum at the end of the contract, based on basic pay and years of service under the labour law. The money is paid once when you leave, not monthly after retirement. The calculator does not include it, since it depends on your contract.

cite.name: Al Meezan, Qatar Labour Law No. 14 of 2004 (end-of-service gratuity)

faq.q: Why do Qataris pay 7% while the employer pays 14%?
faq.a: For nationals, GRSIA is funded by shared contributions. The employee pays 7% and the employer 14%, both on pay up to QAR 100,000 a month. Only the 7% reduces your take-home pay. The 14% is paid on top of your salary and is shown separately.

cite.name: Al Meezan, Qatar Social Insurance Law No. 1 of 2022 (GRSIA contributions, 7% employee, cap 100,000 a month)
TRC, Qatar retirement and pension law: 7% employee, 14% employer, QAR 100,000 monthly ceiling

faq.q: Is there really no income tax in Qatar?
faq.a: Not on salary. The state does not tax employment income for individuals and there is no personal tax return for wages. Your home country may still tax you under its own rules.

cite.name: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Qatar: taxes on personal income

faq.q: Do I need to pay tax at home if I work in Qatar?
faq.a: It depends on your home country, which the calculator does not model. Some countries tax citizens on worldwide income or keep you resident for tax for a time. Check with your home tax authority.

faq.q: What does a Qatar salary buy compared with home?
faq.a: The Cost of Living Comparator shows what a salary buys in another city, which helps when a package includes housing.
